name: Meadows Row
summary: A unilateral landmine row performed standing perpendicular to the barbell with a pronated grip on the sleeve to target the lats and upper back.

setup: Load the sleeve of a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment, preferably using smaller-diameter plates to allow a greater range of motion.
Stand perpendicular to the barbell with a staggered stance, placing the foot on the working side slightly behind the front foot.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly 45 degrees to the floor, bracing your non-working forearm on your front thigh for support.
Grip the thick collar end of the barbell sleeve with an overhand (pronated) grip using the working arm.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow up and slightly out toward your hip.
Row the collar until your elbow reaches or slightly passes torso height, squeezing the lat and upper back.
Lower the barbell under control until your arm is fully extended and you feel a mild stretch in the lat.
Complete the desired repetitions on one side before turning around to repeat on the other side.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight into full extension; exhale forcefully as you drive the elbow up into the row.
cues: Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
Keep your chest proud and hips square.
Let the shoulder blade glide forward at the bottom for a deep stretch.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso rotation or heaving momentum to lift the bar.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders and hips square to the floor and initiate each rep purely from the back muscles.

common_faults.fault: Using 45-pound or Olympic-diameter plates that bump the torso prematurely.
common_faults.correction: Load multiple smaller-diameter plates (such as 25-pound plates) to maximize your pulling range of motion.

precautions: Maintain a neutral spine and brace your core throughout to protect the lower back.
